question: Does the explicit choice-free Krein carrier admit positive normalized states, and does its fundamental symmetry J by itself select a physical state or probability rule?
answer: The state-existence link closes in ZF for the displayed carrier. If v is an explicitly named unit coordinate with Jv=sigma v, then omega_v(A)=sigma[v,Av]=(v,Av)_0 is a positive normalized vector state on the companion Hilbert-adjoint operator algebra, represented by the explicit rank-one density |v><v|_0. The Fock vacuum and every named occupation coordinate give the same kind of state without a choice operation. These states are nonunique. More sharply, no density-operator state on the one-particle carrier is invariant under every finite coordinate permutation preserving the positive and negative J sectors: invariance makes the diagonal weight constant on each explicitly infinite sector, while trace one forces their sum to be one and trace class forces both constants to vanish. Thus J supplies state existence after Hilbertization but does not select a normal permutation-natural state. This does not rule out singular states or selection by energy, dynamics, boundary data, BRST reduction, or another physical principle.

typed_products.typing_boundary: C*-state positivity omega(A^dagger_0 A)>=0 is asserted. Positivity with the Krein adjoint is a different predicate and is not silently substituted.

state_construction.carrier: H_1=l2(I) with the coordinate Hilbert product and J=+1 on E, -1 on A,L
state_construction.positivity_proof: omega_v(A^dagger_0 A)=sigma[v,A^dagger_0 A v]=(v,A^dagger_0 A v)_0=||Av||_0^2>=0.
state_construction.density_operator: rho_v=|v><v|_0 is an explicitly given positive rank-one operator with trace one.
state_construction.boundedness: |omega_v(A)|<=||A|| follows from the coordinate Hilbert product and ||v||_0=1.

fock_state_construction.vacuum: The empty occupation is a named Gamma_s(J)-positive unit coordinate and defines omega_0(A)=<0|A|0>_0.
fock_state_construction.negative_one_particle: Any named one-particle A or L occupation is a Gamma_s(J)-negative unit coordinate and defines the sign-normalized state -[m,A m].
fock_state_construction.nonuniqueness_witness: The vacuum state and a one-particle coordinate state disagree on the vacuum rank-one projection.
fock_state_construction.extra_structure_warning: The vacuum is named by the occupation grading, not selected by J alone, and no dynamics or physical asymptotic condition makes it the Weyl or Bateman-Turok state here.

selection_obstruction.theorem: No positive trace-class density rho of trace one on H_1 is invariant under every finite coordinate permutation that preserves the positive and negative J sectors.
selection_obstruction.scope: density-operator states on the explicit one-particle coordinate carrier
proof: Invariance under finite permutations within the positive E sector makes every positive-sector diagonal entry <e_i,rho e_i>_0 equal to one constant c_+>=0.
Invariance under finite permutations within the negative A/L sector makes every negative-sector diagonal entry equal to one constant c_->=0.
Each sector contains an explicitly enumerated infinite sequence. Positivity and trace one give N c_+<=1 and N c_-<=1 for every natural N, hence c_+=c_-=0.
For a positive trace-class operator, the trace is the sum of its diagonal entries in the supplied coordinate basis. All entries are zero, so tr(rho)=0, contradicting tr(rho)=1.
selection_obstruction.interpretation: A state may be selected only after adding structure that breaks or refines the J-preserving coordinate symmetry, or by leaving the density-operator class.
does_not_rule_out: states selected by the energy operator or a Hamiltonian
KMS, boundary, incoming, detector, or asymptotic selection data
a dynamically justified generalized Born functional

finite_exact_witness.positivity_identity_checked: For every 2x2 integer A in the declared range and v=p,n, omega_v(A^T A)=||Av||_2^2.
finite_exact_witness.control_boundary: Finite uniform density matrices exist at every cutoff. Their coordinate weights tend toward zero and do not define a trace-one density operator on the infinite carrier.

nodes.statement: The explicit l2(I), J, and Fock coordinate carriers exist in ZF.
Positive E and negative A coordinates are explicitly named.
rho_v is explicit, positive, rank one, and trace one.
Vacuum and occupation coordinates give explicit states.
Two coordinate states disagree on a rank-one projection.
Demand invariance under every finite sign-preserving coordinate permutation.
No trace-one positive density operator satisfies G0 on two infinite sectors.
State existence is proved; physical selection and Born interpretation are not.
